BiblicalUsage: To say, the commonest verb in the Bible, four thousand times and more. And God said, Let there be light: and there was light. And God said unto Moses, I AM THAT I AM: thus shalt thou say unto the children of Israel, I AM hath sent me unto you; the word is the saying itself, and the Bible begins with God saying and goes on saying until the end.
TheologicalSignificance: Saying is the commonest act in the Bible, and the word itself teaches nothing; the weight is who says it, that when God says, light is, and when God says I AM, Moses has a name to carry into Egypt.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
